title: isTrustedSender trusts a caller-supplied domain independently of the email, tolerates multi-@ strings, and does no trimming or validation
evidence: isTrustedSender('evil@x.com@ashoka.edu.in', undefined, cfg) is true (domain taken after the LAST @); isTrustedSender('evil@x.com', 'ashoka.edu.in', cfg) is true because the explicit domain argument is never checked against the email's own domain. Safe today only because gws-gmail derives senderDomain from the same string. Reproduced in join-rules.test.ts 'documented deliberate divergence'. Not edited per unit limits.
fix_direction: When the switch-over unit moves the scheduler to evaluateJoinRules, drop the separate domain argument and derive the domain from the validated email; otherwise reject domain/email mismatches in isTrustedSender.
regression_check: Fixed in 451edce (isTrustedSender decides from parseStrictEmail; a supplied domain must equal the email's parsed domain and never grants trust). Checker cycle 1: ISS-CAPTURE-001 recorded reproductions 3/3 refused on an independent probe (3/3 trusted by the pre-fix function from 32349dc); trusted-sender.test.ts 6/6, calendar caller tests green; mutation 9/12 killed, survivors M7 (redundant special-char regex), M11 (320 length cap), M12 (equivalent); real Gmail From shapes all still trusted. Residual: the apps/api senderDomain split path is ISS-CAPTURE-003 (open), sender authentication is ISS-322/333 (open).

title: evaluateJoinRules fails OPEN on invalid rule data: an allow rule whose match.scope is not exactly 'internal'/'external' matches every EXTERNAL sender, contradicting the module's 'invalid values never match (fail-closed for allow)' claim
area: packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/join-rules.ts:ruleMatches (line ~121-124) and the evaluator's trust that the set was validated
evidence: Probe (scratchpad t037-check/probe.ts), ownDomains ['corp.com'], single rule {id:'a',effect:'allow',match:{scope:S}}, sender a@other.com (external), meeting https://meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij, empty state. S in {'Internal','INTERNAL','both','',null,1,true} -> action 'join', reason 'allow-rule' (expected needs-approval); the matching internal sender a@corp.com is NOT joined for the same S, so a one-letter-case typo INVERTS the rule. Cause: `(match.scope === 'internal') !== internal` is true for any non-'internal' value when internal===false. Same class: {domain:'x.com',subdomains:'false'} (string) is treated as subdomains=true and joins a@sub.x.com; an invalid DENY rule ({scope:'Internal'} or {domain:'*.evil.com'}) silently fails to deny so a later allow joins (the maker documents only this deny case). validateJoinRuleSet rejects every one of these, but the evaluator accepts the unvalidated type and the persistence boundary (not built yet) is JSON.
fix_direction: Make the evaluator safe on its own: in ruleMatches treat scope not in {internal,external}, non-boolean subdomains and non-string email/domain/platform as 'invalid' and (allow) never match / (deny) fail closed (skip with a reason like 'invalid-rule-set'), or have evaluateJoinRules accept only a branded ValidatedJoinRuleSet produced by validateJoinRuleSet. Add tests that feed the evaluator the unvalidated bad values above. Correct the manifest/code comment that says allow is fail-closed.
regression_check: Fixed in af90e13 (evaluator runs validateJoinRuleSet/validateJoinRuleState and fails closed with needs-approval/invalid-rule-set). Checker cycle 2: ISS-CAPTURE-002 recorded reproductions 17/17 refused on an independent probe; join-rules.test.ts 24/24; mutations N1-N8 killed.

title: gws-gmail.ts derives senderDomain with senderEmail.split("@")[1] (first-@ segment), inconsistent with the strict email parse now enforced by isTrustedSender
area: apps/api/src/gws-gmail.ts:259 (const senderDomain = senderEmail.split("@")[1] ?? "";) with FROM_RE/extractEmail at ~:114-116
evidence: For From 'x@ashoka.edu.in@evil.com' the upstream senderDomain is 'ashoka.edu.in' while the real domain is evil.com. After ISS-CAPTURE-001's fix isTrustedSender refuses it (a supplied domain must equal the domain parsed from the email, and multi-@ is rejected), so the trust gate no longer depends on this line. The wrong senderDomain is still stored on the candidate and returned by the API/UI and may be used by other consumers (display, de-duplication, trusted_senders approvals by domain).
fix_direction: Wiring needed (apps/api, outside this lane's unit): stop deriving the domain with split; either omit senderDomain and let consumers parse the email, or derive it with the same strict parse (parseStrictEmail exported from packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/join-rules.ts) and drop candidates whose From does not parse. Also audit other readers of senderDomain (trusted-senders DB approvals by domain).
